defects: Third second is nearly dead (per-second change 6.2): the plant/'next water' shot holds almost still with only tiny leaf sway, which reads as dead air
Opening frame is a lone small drop on an empty field; it has no composition and doesn't work as a poster
The gauge's liquid surface is a thin, low-amplitude wobble with no slosh or overshoot when the fill level jumps 31→43→62%, so the liquid has no weight
Caption word 'kitchen' arrives on a dropped baseline with lighter weight and pops into place; the stagger looks like a glitch rather than a choice
The 'well' letters bounce on raised baselines and settle in a uniform, mechanical way with no per-letter overlap visible in the 1/6 s pair
Surfaces are fully flat vector: no grain, no light and no falloff on the gauge sphere or plant; at 100% it reads as a UI kit, not a film
gaps: Energy curve: two busy seconds, then a near-static third, then everything piles into the logo. There's no build to a peak at 60-80% and no deliberate release. The drop→gauge→plant→logo chain needs continuous transforms (the drop becoming the liquid, the liquid feeding the plant) instead of cuts between still compositions

Weight and physics: the hero material is water, but nothing behaves like it. No splash on impact, no slosh or overshoot in the gauge, no squash on the falling drop, no drip timing into the i-dot. Top studios would sell the whole piece on fluid secondary motion

Finish and material: flat fills, no texture, no lighting on the sphere, generic sans captions at small sizes. Adding subtle grain, a meniscus highlight and refraction, and one more deliberate typographic voice would lift it from clean template to authored work
